examples.en: Grandmother embroiders flowers on a handkerchief.

examples.ko: 어머니는 한 땀 한 땀 베개에 이름을 수놓으셨어요.
examples.en: Mother embroidered a name on the pillow stitch by stitch.
The stars dotting the night sky look beautiful.
I bought thread for embroidering in each color.
In autumn the maple leaves paint the mountain red.

examples.ko: 이 가방에는 작은 새가 수놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A little bird is embroidered on this bag.

explain: 천에 바늘과 실로 그림이나 글자를 만들 때 쓰고, '수를 놓다'라고 띄어 쓰기도 해요. 비유로 별, 꽃, 단풍이 가득 퍼진 모습에도 써서 '별이 하늘을 수놓다'라고 해요. 이때는 글이나 방송에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My mother is embroidering a pillow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수놓다'를 띄어 쓴 말로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of 수놓다, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: I got an embroidered handkerchief as a gift from a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄴ'을 붙여 이미 수가 놓인 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -(으)ㄴ ending describes an item that already has embroidery on it.

phrases.en: Stars are adorning the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별, 꽃 등이 가득 퍼진 모습을 비유로 말할 때 쓰고, 글이나 방송에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for stars or flowers spreading across a space, common in writing and broadcasts.

explain_en: It is used for making pictures or letters on cloth with needle and thread, and can also be written as two words, '수를 놓다'. Figuratively it describes stars, flowers or autumn leaves spread across a place, as in '별이 하늘을 수놓다', mostly in writing and broadcasts.

examples.en: Children are riding the seesaw in the park.

examples.ko: 시소는 한 명이 내려가면 다른 사람이 올라가요.
examples.en: On a seesaw, when one person goes down, the other goes up.
I am scared of seesaws, so I can't ride one.

examples.ko: 놀이터에 새로 생긴 시소 앞에 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: There is a long line in front of the new seesaw at the playground.

examples.ko: 시소 위에서 아이 둘이 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: Two kids are laughing on the seesaw.

examples.ko: 우리는 어릴 때 시소로 자주 놀았어요.
examples.en: When we were little, we often played on the seesaw.

explain: '시소를 타다'처럼 '타다'와 같이 써요. 놀이터에서는 '그네를 타다', '미끄럼틀을 타다'도 같은 동사를 써요.

phrases.en: a seesaw game; a closely matched contest
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수를 서로 주고받으며 팽팽하게 이어지는 경기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a game in which both sides keep trading the lead.

explain_en: Say '시소를 타다', using the verb '타다'. At a playground you use the same verb in '그네를 타다' and '미끄럼틀을 타다'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 완벽한 착지로 금메달을 땄어요.
examples.en: That athlete won gold with a perfect landing.
The skydiver's landing was so smooth that I was surprised.

examples.ko: 점프한 뒤에 착지가 불안해서 발목을 다쳤어요.
examples.en: My landing after the jump was unstable, so I hurt my ankle.

examples.ko: 체조 선수들은 착지 연습을 매일 해요.
examples.en: Gymnasts practice their landings every day.

examples.ko: 착지 장소가 너무 좁아서 위험해 보여요.
examples.en: The landing spot is so narrow that it looks dangerous.

examples.ko: 스키 점프는 착지 자세에 따라 점수가 달라져요.
examples.en: In ski jumping, the score changes depending on the landing posture.

explain: 착지는 점프나 비행이 끝나고 땅에 닿는 순간이라 체조, 스키, 항공 이야기에 많이 나와요. 비행기는 보통 '착륙'을 더 자주 써요. '착지'는 발이나 몸이 닿는 모습에 초점이 있어요.

phrases.example: 선수가 어려운 점프 뒤에 착지에 성공했어요.
phrases.en: The athlete landed successfully after a hard jump.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점프 뒤 넘어지지 않고 잘 내려온 경우에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone lands well without falling after a jump.

phrases.en: You need a good landing posture so you don't get hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅에 닿을 때의 몸 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the body position when touching the ground.

phrases.example: 마지막 착지 실수 때문에 점수가 깎였어요.
phrases.en: Points were deducted because of a mistake in the final landing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 경기에서 잘못 내려온 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a mistake when landing in sports.

explain_en: 착지 is the moment you touch the ground after a jump or flight, so it appears a lot in gymnastics, skiing and flying. For airplanes 착륙 is more common. 착지 focuses on how the feet or body come down.

examples.en: The athlete landed safely on both feet.
The parachute lands gently on the grass.

examples.ko: 점프하고 한 발로 착지하면 무릎이 위험해요.
examples.en: Landing on one foot after a jump is risky for your knee.

examples.ko: 우리 고양이는 높은 곳에서 떨어져도 잘 착지해요.
examples.en: Our cat lands well even when it falls from a high place.
A bird landed lightly on the branch.
You have to bend your knees the moment you land.

explain: 사람이나 동물이 뛰어내린 뒤 발이 땅에 닿을 때 착지하다를 써요. '바닥에 착지하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 말해요. 비행기가 활주로에 내리는 일은 '착륙하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I jumped high but landed safely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다치지 않고 안전하게 내려왔을 때 '무사히'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 무사히 with it when someone lands safely without getting hurt.

phrases.en: My foot slipped, so I couldn't land properly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 내려오지 못했을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for when someone fails to land well.

phrases.en: I bend my knees a little when I land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 때'를 붙여 내려오는 순간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -ㄹ 때 to talk about the moment of landing.

explain_en: 착지하다 is for people or animals whose feet touch the ground after jumping down; it goes with 에, as in '바닥에 착지하다'. When a plane comes down on a runway, 착륙하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: I tried hanging from the bar at the park.

examples.ko: 철봉 운동을 하고 나서 팔이 아파요.
examples.en: My arms hurt after working out on the bar.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 철봉에서 턱걸이를 못 해요.
examples.en: I still can't do a pull-up on the bar.
The kids grabbed the bar and hung upside down.

examples.ko: 철봉이 높아서 아이가 손이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: The bar is high, so the child can't reach it.
I'm building arm strength with the bar.

explain: 놀이터나 공원, 학교 운동장에 있는 가로 막대예요. '철봉에 매달리다', '철봉 운동', '턱걸이'와 같이 자주 나와요. 체조 종목 이름으로도 써요.

phrases.en: I did ten pull-ups on the bar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철봉을 잡고 몸을 끌어올리는 운동 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The exercise of pulling yourself up on the bar.

phrases.example: 철봉을 꽉 잡고 몸을 들어 올렸어요.
phrases.en: I gripped the bar tightly and lifted myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동을 시작할 때 손으로 철봉을 쥐는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of gripping the bar to start.

phrases.en: The children are playing on the horizontal bar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이터에서 철봉을 이용해 노는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes kids playing on the bar at a playground.

explain_en: It is the horizontal bar found at playgrounds, parks and school fields. It often appears with '철봉에 매달리다', '철봉 운동' and '턱걸이' (pull-up). It is also the name of a gymnastics event.

examples.en: The forward fell from the defender's tackle.

examples.ko: 너무 깊은 태클이라서 심판이 카드를 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: It was such a hard tackle that the referee pulled out a card.

examples.ko: 태클을 잘하는 선수가 팀에 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: A player who tackles well is essential to the team.

examples.ko: 새 계획에 태클이 들어와서 일이 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: Someone objected to the new plan, so the work got delayed.
I waited for the right timing to tackle and win the ball.
Tackles are dangerous on slippery grass.

explain: 축구에서 발로 상대의 공을 빼앗는 동작이지만, 일상에서는 남의 일에 시비를 걸고 막을 때도 많이 써요. 경기에서는 '태클을 하다', 방해할 때는 '태클을 걸다'로 동사가 달라요.

phrases.example: 회의에서 계속 태클을 거는 사람이 있어요.
phrases.en: pick on someone; obstruct
phrases.nuance_ko: 축구 태클처럼 상대를 막아서, 말이나 행동으로 시비를 걸고 일을 방해할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like a soccer tackle that stops an opponent, it means to nitpick or get in someone's way with words or actions.

explain_en: In soccer it is the move of taking the ball away with your foot, but in daily life it is also used when someone picks on or blocks another person's plans. In a match you say 태클을 하다, and for obstruction the verb changes to 태클을 걸다.

examples.en: The children played in the river, swimming around.
A duck is swimming slowly on the lake.

examples.ko: 헤엄에 자신이 없어서 깊은 곳에는 안 가요.
examples.en: I'm not confident at swimming, so I don't go to deep places.

examples.ko: 헤엄도 못 치는데 바다에 가자고 해요.
examples.en: He wants to go to the sea even though I can't swim.
He moved his arms and legs as if a frog were swimming.

examples.ko: 물이 차가워서 헤엄이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: The water is cold, so I can't swim well.

explain: '헤엄'은 사람, 동물, 물고기에게 모두 쓰고 '헤엄을 치다'라고 해요. 운동으로 하는 건 '수영'이라고 해서 '수영 대회'는 되지만 '헤엄 대회'는 어색해요. 놀이나 동물 이야기에 '헤엄'을 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Fish swim in the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헤엄'에 '치다'를 붙여 한 낱말 동사로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 치다 to 헤엄 makes a single verb.

phrases.en: I learned to swim in the summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에서 몸을 움직여 나아가는 방법을 익힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for learning how to move through water.

phrases.en: My younger sibling swims well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤엄 실력을 말할 때 '잘/못'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 잘 or 못 to talk about swimming ability.

explain_en: '헤엄' is used for people, animals, and fish, and the verb phrase is '헤엄을 치다'. Swimming as a sport is '수영', so '수영 대회' works but '헤엄 대회' sounds odd. '헤엄' is common in talk about play and animals.

examples.en: A small stream runs through the middle of the city.
Children are splashing in the stream.
When it rains, the stream swells.
I walked along the path beside the stream.

examples.ko: 개천 물이 맑아서 작은 물고기가 보여요.
examples.en: The stream water is clear, so I can see small fish.
Cherry blossoms bloomed along the stream.

explain: '강'보다 작고 '시내', '냇물'과 비슷한 곳을 가리켜요. 도시에서는 '청계천'처럼 '천'이 붙은 이름이 많고, 말할 때는 '개천'이 가장 쉬운 말이에요.

phrases.example: 가난한 집 아이가 의사가 되다니, 개천에서 용 났네요.
phrases.en: A dragon rises from the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 환경에서 훌륭한 사람이 나왔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when someone from a humble background becomes very successful.

explain_en: It is smaller than a '강' and close to '시내' and '냇물'. In cities many streams have names ending in '천', like '청계천', but in speech '개천' is the easiest word.

examples.en: There is a spider web in the corner of the window.
Morning dew glistened on the spider web.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 안 쓴 창고에는 거미줄이 가득했어요.
examples.en: The storage room, unused for a long time, was full of cobwebs.
I swept away the cobwebs with a broom.
A small bug got caught in the web.

examples.ko: 거미줄 모양 과자가 신기해서 사 봤어요.
examples.en: I bought a web-shaped snack because it looked interesting.

explain: 거미가 만든 줄이에요. 거미가 집을 짓는 것은 '거미줄을 치다', 사람이 걷어 내는 것은 '거미줄을 걷어 내다'라고 해요. 오래 안 쓴 곳을 말할 때 '거미줄이 쳐져 있다'고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: A small bug got caught in the spider web.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레나 먼지가 거미줄에 붙었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a bug or dust gets stuck in a web.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in a spider web

phrases.en: While cleaning I removed the spider webs from the ceiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 청소할 때 거미줄을 없애는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of a person clearing webs while cleaning.
phrases.en_equiv: to clear away a spider web

phrases.example: 오래 비워 둔 방에 거미줄이 쳐져 있었어요.
phrases.en: There were spider webs in the room that had been empty for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치다'의 피동 표현으로, 거미줄이 생긴 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 치다, describing the state of webs having formed.

explain_en: The spider spins its web with 거미줄을 치다, and a person clears it with 거미줄을 걷어 내다. A common phrase for a place left unused is 거미줄이 쳐져 있다.

examples.en: Long icicles hang from the edge of the eaves.

examples.ko: 아침 햇볕에 고드름이 녹아서 물이 떨어져요.
examples.en: The icicles melt in the morning sun and water drips down.
I can hear the sound of icicles melting and trickling.
The kids snapped off icicles and played with them.
Be careful, because falling icicles are dangerous.
When winter comes, icicles form on the roof.

explain: '고드름이 달리다, 얼다, 녹다'처럼 함께 써요. 손으로 떼어 낼 때는 '고드름을 따다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Icicles are hanging from the edge of the roof.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고드름이 매달려 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes icicles hanging down.

phrases.en: The weather got warmer, so the icicles are melting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울이 끝나 갈 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as winter comes to an end.

phrases.en: The kids break off icicles and play with them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 떼어 낼 때 '따다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 따다 is used when you snap them off by hand.

explain_en: It pairs with '달리다', '얼다' and '녹다'. When you snap one off by hand, you say '고드름을 따다'.

examples.en: A pheasant suddenly flew up on the mountain path.
A pheasant's call can be heard loudly even from far away.
I saw a pheasant in the field.
In the past people sometimes made dumplings with pheasant meat.

examples.ko: 꿩 깃털로 장식한 모자를 박물관에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a hat decorated with pheasant feathers at the museum.
The kids were amazed to see a pheasant.

explain: 산이나 들에 사는 큰 새라서 도시에서는 보기 어려워요. 속담에도 자주 나오는 새예요. 아래 '이렇게도 써요'의 두 속담은 일상에서도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 방법이면 꿩 먹고 알 먹기예요.
phrases.en: This way, it's killing two birds with one stone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일로 이익을 두 가지 얻을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one action brings two benefits.
phrases.en_equiv: kill two birds with one stone

phrases.example: 원하는 색이 없어서 꿩 대신 닭으로 다른 색을 샀어요.
phrases.en: The color I wanted was out, so I bought another color as a second best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 것이 없을 때 비슷한 다른 것으로 대신한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means settling for a similar substitute when the thing you want isn't available.

explain_en: It is a large bird that lives in mountains and fields, so it is hard to see in cities. It also shows up in proverbs. The two proverbs under '이렇게도 써요' are used a lot in daily life.

examples.en: Ants find their way with their antennae.
The butterfly's antennae quivered.
The snail pulled its feelers right in.

examples.ko: 곤충 더듬이는 냄새를 맡는 일도 해요.
examples.en: Insect antennae also help them smell.
I found an insect with long antennae in the field guide.
The child closely observed the bug's antennae.

explain: 곤충이나 달팽이 머리에 달려 주변을 느끼는 부분에 써요. '더듬다'에서 온 말이라 손으로 더듬듯 주변을 살핀다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고 '더듬이가 길다/떨리다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: This insect has long antennae.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충의 생김새를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe an insect's appearance.

phrases.en: The ant walks along moving its antennae.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변을 살피는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of sensing the surroundings.

phrases.en: I lightly touched the snail's feelers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달팽이에게도 '더듬이'라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word is also used for snails.

explain_en: It is used for the part on the head of an insect or snail that senses its surroundings. It comes from '더듬다' (to grope), giving the feel of probing around like a hand. It isn't used for people; you say '더듬이가 길다/떨리다'.

examples.ko: 말벌에 쏘이면 크게 부을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get stung by a hornet, it can swell up a lot.

examples.ko: 처마 밑에 말벌 집이 생겨서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: A hornet nest formed under the eaves, and I was scared.
Hornets are much bigger and more aggressive than honeybees.

examples.ko: 가을에 산에 갈 때는 말벌을 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful of hornets when you go to the mountains in autumn.

examples.ko: 말벌이 방 안으로 들어와서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: A hornet came into the room, so I opened the window.
The firefighters were dispatched because of hornets.

explain: '꿀벌'은 꿀을 모으는 순한 벌이고, 말벌은 몸집이 크고 독이 강한 벌이에요. 가을에 산에 가면 말벌 주의 안내가 자주 나와요. 벌에 쏘이는 건 '벌에 쏘이다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I found a hornet's nest in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 처음 보게 되었을 때 '발견하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '발견하다' is used when you first notice the nest.

phrases.en: A hornet flew in through the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌이 가까이 올 때 '날아오다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '날아오다' when a bee or wasp comes close.

phrases.en: Be careful of hornets in the mountains in fall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 경고에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in notices and warnings.

explain_en: 꿀벌 is the gentle bee that collects honey, while 말벌 is a large hornet with strong venom. Warnings about 말벌 often appear in autumn when people go hiking. Getting stung by a bee is said as 벌에 쏘이다.

examples.en: The kids are kicking a ball on the bare ground.
It rained, so the bare ground became muddy.
If you sit on the bare ground, your bottom gets cold.
The playground was bare ground with not a blade of grass.
This flower grows well even on bare ground.
It was hard to pitch a tent on the bare ground.

explain: 풀이나 바닥재 없이 흙이 그대로 드러난 땅이에요. 집 안 바닥에는 보통 '맨바닥'을 쓰고, '맨땅'은 밖의 흙땅에 써요. '맨-'은 아무것도 덮이거나 더해지지 않았다는 뜻으로 '맨손, 맨발'에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 아무 경험 없이 가게를 열어서 맨땅에 헤딩하는 기분이에요.
phrases.en: I opened a shop with no experience, so it feels like I'm starting from nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비나 도움 없이 처음부터 무작정 부딪쳐 보는 상황에 써요. 주로 말할 때 쓰는 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you take on something from zero with no preparation or help. Mostly colloquial.
phrases.en_equiv: start from scratch; go in blind

explain_en: It is ground where the soil is exposed, with no grass or paving. For floors inside a building people usually say '맨바닥', while '맨땅' is for outdoor soil. The prefix '맨-' means nothing is covering or added, as in 맨손 and 맨발.
